**Unblocked — `Blocked-by: #6431` resolves.**

#6431 closed `completed`: *"[finding] app-shell's two action runtimes reset `paramState` differently when ActionParamDialog …"*. That was the hot-file serialization on the `ActionParamDialog` seam this card was waiting behind.

Returned to `pm:queue`. Re-measure the file face on the merged ref before dispatching: this card names a **third** `ActionParamDialog` consumer, and #6431's fix landed on the other two — so whether the third still diverges, and in which direction, is a measurement on `main` now, not a fact carried over from when the card was filed.

Claim: PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat, objectui). Branch `claude/issue-6473-metadatatypeactions-paramstate`. Dispatched this round to one `os-dev` agent, in its own worktree.

Premise re-measured on `main` before dispatching, since this card was `pm:blocked` behind #6431 until an hour ago and the merge that closed an upstream is the one most likely to have swept its dependants. It did not: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/MetadataTypeActions.tsx` still carries `:115 setParamState({ open: true, params, title, resolve })` against `:245 setParamState({ open: false, params: [] })`. The card's line numbers are exact on `main`, which is unusual enough to be worth saying — the dispatch still asks the implementer to re-measure rather than trust them.

On the sub-decision this card names — whether the `paramState.resolve?.(null)` line stays once the state stops being blanked — the dispatch authorises **both** answers and requires the measurement to pick. It does not pre-answer it.

Hot-file note for any seat reading this: `MetadataTypeActions.tsx` is serialized on this claim until the PR lands. `ActionParamDialog.tsx` itself is read-only for this card.

**Sub-decision — the `paramState.resolve?.(null)` line: DROPPED.** Paths enumerated, all of them into `onOpenChange(false)`, all inside `ActionParamDialog` (read-only for this card, unchanged):

1. `handleSubmit` (`ActionParamDialog.tsx:280-281`) — `state.resolve?.(serializeParamValues(...))`, then `onOpenChange(false)`.
2. `handleCancel` (`:285-286`) — `state.resolve?.(null)`, then `onOpenChange(false)`.
3. The Radix root's own `onOpenChange` (`:295-297`), which delegates to `handleCancel`. This is the single route taken by **Escape**, an **overlay/outside click** and the **header X button** — `DialogContent` renders a `DialogPrimitive.Close` that flips the root.

The host never calls the prop itself, and `setParamState` occurs in exactly two places in the file (open at `:115`, close in the JSX), so there is no fourth way in. No path arrives unsettled; on the submit path the removed line was additionally a `null` settle layered over a values settle, i.e. the wrong intent had it ever been load-bearing. Not asserted but executable: the new test drives all four routes through the real component and asserts `resolve` precedes `onOpenChange(false)` in each, plus a census over `ActionParamDialog.tsx` (exactly two direct `onOpenChange(` calls, each preceded by a settle; exactly one `onOpenChange={` prop, delegating to `handleCancel`) so a fifth, unsettled call site added later is red there rather than a promise pending forever.

Gate status at report time is as recorded above; CI convergence on PR #6586 is the PM's read.

**Post-merge verification — PR #6586 merged 2026-08-26T16:39:01Z. Measured on `main`, clean.**

**The fix.** `MetadataTypeActions.tsx:281` — `if (!open) setParamState((s) => ({ ...s, open: false }));`. The field-preserving shape, matching what `useConsoleActionRuntime` and `RecordDetailView` already had.

**`resolve?.(null)` is gone from the code.** Its only two surviving occurrences (`:264`, `:270`) are prose inside the `{/* … */}` block that closes at `:277` — the explanation of *why* it was dropped and which paths settle. That is what stops a future reader restoring it as an apparent oversight.

⚠️ Worth recording: this seat's first pass classified those two as **code**, because the heuristic tested for a leading `*` and a block-comment line need not have one. The underlying fact was clean; the classifier was not. Same failure family as the other instrument slips logged today, and again in the direction that manufactures a finding rather than hiding one.

**⛔ The read-only exclusion held.** `ActionParamDialog.tsx` is untouched and its settle sites are intact:

```
:280   state.resolve?.(serializeParamValues(visibleParams, values));
:281   onOpenChange(false);
:285   state.resolve?.(null);
:286   onOpenChange(false);
```

Those are the paths the enumeration rests on, and they are exactly as they were — the third consumer converged onto the dialog's contract rather than the dialog being bent to fit it.

Nothing outstanding on this card.
